newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN MINISTER BEMOANS MANPOWER SPENT ON QUERY.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN MINISTER BEMOANS MANPOWER SPENT ON QUERY.

text.p: It took 60 man days to answer one parliamentary question last year and it would be wasteful to do the calculations again, South African Transport Minister Mac Maharaj said in a written answer to a parliamentary question.

Maharaj declined to update his answer to a question from Democratic Party Senator James Selfe, who asked how many consultants the department had hired, what their qualifications were and what they were paid.
"I think I can fairly claim that my department's practice over the last two years has clearly demonstrated our commitment to transparency and accountability," the minister said.
Maharaj said it had taken six officials two full weeks to answer the question last year, tracking 75 advisers and consultants and seven companies hired for advice.
"I am concerned about the dissipation of energies occasioned by the need to respond to complex repeat questions on an annual basis," he said.
Maharaj said the answer had "not changed substantially" since August last year, when Selfe asked the same question.
